blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          e…

🚨 **BLOCKING: CI `crap` quality gate is red — 3 new functions over `CRAP_THRESHOLD=8`**

The unit suite is green (reproduced locally: 4333 passed / 0 failed, matching the PR description), but the failed `crap` check is the CRAP ratchet, and the job log (fetched via `gh run view 39154646821 --log-failed`) shows:

```
CRAP Ratchet
============
NEW > 8  js/common/reviewSpecClaims.js::sanitizeReviewData: 23
NEW > 8  js/unit-tests/test_postPRReviewComments.js::loadWithFileMap: 23.4
NEW > 8  js/unit-tests/test_postPRReviewComments.js::file_read#10: 8.7
0 regression(s), 3 new over threshold, 0 improvement(s), 0 removed
```

`classifyFindingSeverity` (CC 23, fully covered → CRAP 23) exceeds the threshold on complexity alone: the ratchet only admits new functions with CRAP ≤ 8, so no coverage percentage can save a CC > 8 function. Please split it — e.g. extract per-comment resolution (`body`/`comment` + `readText`), per-comment demotion application, and census/verdict rebalancing into separate ≤ 8-CC helpers.

The test side needs slimming too: `loadWithFileMap` (CC 23.4) duplicates the entire require-map construction — extract a shared `requireMap()` helper used by both it and the existing loaders, and collapse the nested `file_read` factories (the CC 8.7 `file_read#10`) into one small resolver function reused at both call sites.

Note for verification: `nyc instrument` + `crap4js --baseline` reproduces the verdict locally (install `github:IstiN/crap4js#83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d` + `nyc@17` as in `.github/workflows/quality.yml`).

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: incidental spec mentions demote genuine BLOCKING bugs — verdict can collapse to APPROVE with a real defect outstanding**

The demotion predicate fires when the body *contains* any spec-claim phrase, regardless of whether that phrase is the finding's core claim. Verified against the shipped regexes:

```
body = '🚨 BLOCKING: SQL injection via raw string interpolation — user input reaches
        the DB unescaped. (Also, the spec says prepared statements are required.)'
isUncitedSpecClaim(body) === true   // → demoted to IMPORTANT, verdict → APPROVE
```

So a review that correctly identifies a security blocker, and incidentally mentions what "the spec says" without a `file:line`, is silently neutered: the 🚨 marker is rewritten, the census drains, and `REQUEST_CHANGES` collapses to `APPROVE` — the exact failure direction the machine cannot afford (a real bug merges while the guard "protects" against a false claim).

This is the inverse of the hostage problem gh-1053 fixes, and arguably worse: a false BLOCKING costs rework cycles, a missed real BLOCKING ships a defect. At minimum, demote only when the spec-claim regex matches *before* any code-level defect evidence, or require that no other BLOCKING marker sentence exists in the body. Ideally the classifier should treat "uncited spec claim" as demoting **the spec-claim portion**, not the whole finding.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: citation detection misses `#L61`-style line anchors (AC4) and accepts any URL**

Two asymmetric gaps in `CITATION_RES`, both verified against the shipped regexes:

1. **False negative — cited claims lose BLOCKING force (violates AC4).** GitHub-permalink style citations, the most common form in review threads, are not recognized:

   ```
   hasVerifiableCitation('deviation from the reference (Policy.java#L61)') === false
   hasVerifiableCitation('deviation (Policy.java:61-66)')                 === true
   ```

   A leg that did read the source and cited `Policy.java#L61` gets its verified finding demoted — precisely the strictness cut AC4 says this must not be.

2. **False positive — any URL counts as a citation.** `https?:\/\/[^\s)<>\]]+` matches *any* link, so "the spec says X is forbidden (see https://example.com/anything)" keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force with zero source verification. The leg can satisfy the guard by pasting an unrelated URL.

Suggested fix: add an anchor alternative to the file pattern — e.g. `[A-Za-z0-9_.\-\/]+\.(?:java|…|md)#[LA]?\d+` — and, if feasible, restrict the URL arm to the actual source hosts the deployment trusts (or at least require the URL to sit on the same line as the spec-claim phrase).

💡 **SUGGESTION: two inline comments referencing the same file double-count the downgrade**

When two `inlineComments` entries point at the same `comment` file, each pass through the loop pushes its own rewrite and increments `downgrades` — verified:

```
same file twice: downgrades=2 rewrites=2 blocking=0 important=2
```

Consequences: `issueCounts.blocking` is decremented twice and `important` incremented twice for one physical comment, and the second `writeFile` silently overwrites the first (harmless here since both bodies carry the note, but the census drift is real and the machine cross-checks the census).

Consider memoizing by `c.comment` (first demotion wins, subsequent same-file entries get severity demoted without an extra census move), or grouping rewrites by path before returning.

💡 **SUGGESTION: note says "confirm against the cited source" — but the whole point is there is no citation**

`DOWNGRADE_NOTE` ends with: *"Please confirm against the cited source; if confirmed, re-raise with a verifiable citation and it regains blocking force."*

"the cited source" reads as if a citation exists; the demotion happened precisely because none did. Rephrase to reference what the finding actually named, e.g.: *"Please confirm against the source the finding references ('<source>'); if confirmed, re-raise with a verifiable citation (file:line / doc URL) and it regains blocking force."* — ideally interpolating the spec-claim phrase that matched so the author knows exactly what to verify.

💡 **SUGGESTION: misaligned indentation on the added require mappings**

The added `'./common/reviewSpecClaims.js'` lines are indented deeper than their sibling keys in the require map (e.g. here, and repeated at lines ~375, ~669, ~978, ~1358, ~2139, ~2472):

```javascript
            './common/reviewVerdicts.js': loadModule('js/common/reviewVerdicts.js', makeRequire({}), {}),
                './common/reviewSpecClaims.js': loadModule('js/common/reviewSpecClaims.js', makeRequire({}), {})
```

Align them with the `'./common/reviewVerdicts.js'` line. Relatedly, the repetition of this mapping in ~8 loaders is itself what pushed `loadWithFileMap`'s CRAP to 23.4 (see the blocking comment) — a single shared `prReviewRequireMap()` helper would fix both the style and the ratchet.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          e…

1. base
2. if (!reviewData)

That's about 13-14. Even with 100% coverage, CRAP = C ≈ 13 > 8 → new function above threshold → ratchet FAILS. Hmm, but wait — coverage: are all branches covered? The 18 tests cover a lot. With coverage c, CRAP = C²(1-c)³ + C. If C=13, need (1-c)³ ≤ (8-13)/169 → negative → impossible. So any function with complexity > 8 and full coverage has CRAP > 8. Threshold 8 with full coverage means complexity ≤ 8 required for new functions.

Hmm wait, but then how does any new function with complexity > 8 ever get merged? Because CRAP_THRESHOLD applies to functions NOT in baseline — the ratchet only fails when CRAP GREW or NEW function EXCEDS threshold. So new functions must have CRAP ≤ 8 at merge time. `classifyFindingSeverity` (CC 23, fully covered → CRAP 23) exceeds the threshold on complexity alone: the ratchet only admits new functions with CRAP ≤ 8, so no coverage percentage can save a CC > 8 function. {"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: incidental spec mentions demote genuine BLOCKING bugs — verdict can collapse to APPROVE with a real defect outstanding**

The demotion predicate fires when the body *contains* any spec-claim phrase, regardless of whether that phrase is the finding's core claim. Verified against the shipped regexes:

```
body = '🚨 BLOCKING: SQL injection via raw string interpolation — user input reaches
        the DB unescaped. (Also, the spec says prepared statements are required.)'
isUncitedSpecClaim(body) === true   // → demoted to IMPORTANT, verdict → APPROVE
```

So a review that correctly identifies a security blocker, and incidentally mentions what "the spec says" without a `file:line`, is silently neutered: the 🚨 marker is rewritten, the census drains, and `REQUEST_CHANGES` collapses to `APPROVE` — the exact failure direction the machine cannot afford (a real bug merges while the guard "protects" against a false claim).

This is the inverse of the hostage problem gh-1053 fixes, and arguably worse: a false BLOCKING costs rework cycles, a missed real BLOCKING ships a defect. At minimum, demote only when the spec-claim regex matches *before* any code-level defect evidence, or require that no other BLOCKING marker sentence exists in the body. Ideally the classifier should treat "uncited spec claim" as demoting **the spec-claim portion**, not the whole finding.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: citation detection misses `#L61`-style line anchors (AC4) and accepts any URL**

Two asymmetric gaps in `CITATION_RES`, both verified against the shipped regexes:

1. **False negative — cited claims lose BLOCKING force (violates AC4).** GitHub-permalink style citations, the most common form in review threads, are not recognized:

   ```
   hasVerifiableCitation('deviation from the reference (Policy.java#L61)') === false
   hasVerifiableCitation('deviation (Policy.java:61-66)')                 === true
   ```

   A leg that did read the source and cited `Policy.java#L61` gets its verified finding demoted — precisely the strictness cut AC4 says this must not be.

2. **False positive — any URL counts as a citation.** `https?:\/\/[^\s)<>\]]+` matches *any* link, so "the spec says X is forbidden (see https://example.com/anything)" keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force with zero source verification. The leg can satisfy the guard by pasting an unrelated URL.

Suggested fix: add an anchor alternative to the file pattern — e.g. `[A-Za-z0-9_.\-\/]+\.(?:java|…|md)#[LA]?\d+` — and, if feasible, restrict the URL arm to the actual source hosts the deployment trusts (or at least require the URL to sit on the same line as the spec-claim phrase).
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: two inline comments referencing the same file double-count the downgrade**

When two `inlineComments` entries point at the same `comment` file, each pass through the loop pushes its own rewrite and increments `downgrades` — verified:

```
same file twice: downgrades=2 rewrites=2 blocking=0 important=2
```

Consequences: `issueCounts.blocking` is decremented twice and `important` incremented twice for one physical comment, and the second `writeFile` silently overwrites the first (harmless here since both bodies carry the note, but the census drift is real and the machine cross-checks the census).

Consider memoizing by `c.comment` (first demotion wins, subsequent same-file entries get severity demoted without an extra census move), or grouping rewrites by path before returning.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment4.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: note says "confirm against the cited source" — but the whole point is there is no citation**

`DOWNGRADE_NOTE` ends with: *"Please confirm against the cited source; if confirmed, re-raise with a verifiable citation and it regains blocking force."*

"the cited source" reads as if a citation exists; the demotion happened precisely because none did. Rephrase to reference what the finding actually named, e.g.: *"Please confirm against the source the finding references ('<source>'); if confirmed, re-raise with a verifiable citation (file:line / doc URL) and it regains blocking force."* — ideally interpolating the spec-claim phrase that matched so the author knows exactly what to verify.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment5.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: misaligned indentation on the added require mappings**

The added `'./common/reviewSpecClaims.js'` lines are indented deeper than their sibling keys in the require map (e.g. here, and repeated at lines ~375, ~669, ~978, ~1358, ~2139, ~2472):

```javascript

                './common/reviewSpecClaims.js': loadModule('js/common/reviewSpecClaims.js', makeRequire({}), {})
```

Align them with the `'./common/reviewVerdicts.js'` line. Relatedly, the repetition of this mapping in ~8 loaders is itself what pushed `loadWithFileMap`'s CRAP to 23.4 (see the blocking comment) — a single shared `prReviewRequireMap()` helper would fix both the style and the ratchet.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          e…

Also note: interestingly, `sanitizeReviewData` CRAP = 23 — full coverage. To get under 8, split into functions each with CC ≤ 8.

Now let me finish the review:

1. CI failure (crap ratchet) — BLOCKING, with exact functions. Verified by fetching the CI log.

2. Findings on the code:

a) **False-positive demotion risk**: `isUncitedSpecClaim` triggers on ANY spec-claim phrase in the body, even incidental. A genuinely blocking finding (e.g. SQL injection) that also mentions "the spec says X" without citation would be demoted to non-blocking and verdict collapsed to APPROVE. The regex families are broad ("the Java policy requires..." pattern). E.g. "🚨 BLOCKING: SQL injection... the framework docs say prepared statements are required" → demoted. Real bug neutered silently. This is a design risk. Severity: IMPORTANT (arguably BLOCKING?). It violates the machine invariant "a BLOCKING entry... the machine cross-checks" — actually the anti-pattern in verdict rules says don't downgrade real bugs. Given the guard is intentionally conservative... I'd flag as IMPORTANT with recommendation: only demote when the spec claim appears to be the core claim, or at minimum require the spec-claim phrase to appear before any other substantive issue... hard. At least flag it.

b) **Citation regex misses plausible citation formats**: `Policy.java#L61` (GitHub line anchor), "Policy.java lines 61-66", `Policy.java:61–66` with en-dash (colon-digit still matches `:61`), "see Policy.java:61" fine. `file.java#L61` — `.java` followed by `#L61` — the regex requires `:\d+` right after extension → `#L61` doesn't match → a cited claim using GitHub permalink style gets demoted. Also bare URLs to the source file without line... Actually URLs count as citations (any http URL counts — even a link to unrelated docs, over-permissive on the other side! e.g. "the spec says X [see our wiki](https://...)" — any URL counts as citation, even if it doesn't support the claim. Over-broad the other direction: keeps BLOCKING force). Both directions of imperfection. SUGESTION: support `#L\d+` anchors.

c) **Duplicate file-referenced comments**: two inlineComments referencing the same file → two rewrites; each `downgradeBody` applied to original content (both contain note — fine), but `out.downgrades` counts 2 → census blocking −2, important +2 for one physical comment. Also last write wins — fine. Minor accounting inaccuracy. SUGESTION.

d) **`classifyFindingSeverity` returns `severity: sev` lowercase** for non-downgraded — unused by caller; fine, no comment needed.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: incidental spec mentions demote genuine BLOCKING bugs — verdict can collapse to APPROVE with a real defect outstanding**

The demotion predicate fires when the body *contains* any spec-claim phrase, regardless of whether that phrase is the finding's core claim. Verified against the shipped regexes:

```
body = '🚨 BLOCKING: SQL injection via raw string interpolation — user input reaches
        the DB unescaped. (Also, the spec says prepared statements are required.)'
isUncitedSpecClaim(body) === true   // → demoted to IMPORTANT, verdict → APPROVE
```

So a review that correctly identifies a security blocker, and incidentally mentions what "the spec says" without a `file:line`, is silently neutered: the 🚨 marker is rewritten, the census drains, and `REQUEST_CHANGES` collapses to `APPROVE` — the exact failure direction the machine cannot afford (a real bug merges while the guard "protects" against a false claim).

This is the inverse of the hostage problem gh-1053 fixes, and arguably worse: a false BLOCKING costs rework cycles, a missed real BLOCKING ships a defect. At minimum, demote only when the spec-claim regex matches *before* any code-level defect evidence, or require that no other BLOCKING marker sentence exists in the body. Ideally the classifier should treat "uncited spec claim" as demoting **the spec-claim portion**, not the whole finding.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: citation detection misses `#L61`-style line anchors (AC4) and accepts any URL**

Two asymmetric gaps in `CITATION_RES`, both verified against the shipped regexes:

1. **False negative — cited claims lose BLOCKING force (violates AC4).** GitHub-permalink style citations, the most common form in review threads, are not recognized:

   ```
   hasVerifiableCitation('deviation from the reference (Policy.java#L61)') === false
   hasVerifiableCitation('deviation (Policy.java:61-66)')                 === true
   ```

   A leg that did read the source and cited `Policy.java#L61` gets its verified finding demoted — precisely the strictness cut AC4 says this must not be.

2. **False positive — any URL counts as a citation.** `https?:\/\/[^\s)<>\]]+` matches *any* link, so "the spec says X is forbidden (see https://example.com/anything)" keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force with zero source verification. The leg can satisfy the guard by pasting an unrelated URL.

Suggested fix: add an anchor alternative to the file pattern — e.g. `[A-Za-z0-9_.\-\/]+\.(?:java|…|md)#[LA]?\d+` — and, if feasible, restrict the URL arm to the actual source hosts the deployment trusts (or at least require the URL to sit on the same line as the spec-claim phrase).
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: two inline comments referencing the same file double-count the downgrade**

When two `inlineComments` entries point at the same `comment` file, each pass through the loop pushes its own rewrite and increments `downgrades` — verified:

```
same file twice: downgrades=2 rewrites=2 blocking=0 important=2
```

Consequences: `issueCounts.blocking` is decremented twice and `important` incremented twice for one physical comment, and the second `writeFile` silently overwrites the first (harmless here since both bodies carry the note, but the census drift is real and the machine cross-checks the census).

Consider memoizing by `c.comment` (first demotion wins, subsequent same-file entries get severity demoted without an extra census move), or grouping rewrites by path before returning.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment4.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: note says "confirm against the cited source" — but the whole point is there is no citation**

`DOWNGRADE_NOTE` ends with: *"Please confirm against the cited source; if confirmed, re-raise with a verifiable citation and it regains blocking force."*

"the cited source" reads as if a citation exists; the demotion happened precisely because none did. ## Review Summary — PR #1058 (gh-1053)

**Verdict: REQUEST_CHANGES** (1 blocking, 2 important, 3 suggestions)

**Key findings:**

1. 🚨 **BLOCKING — CI `crap` quality gate is red.** The PR description claims "Full suite: 433 passed" (I reproduced 4333/4333 green locally), but the failed `crap` check is the CRAP ratchet. I fetched the real job log via `gh` (the prepared `ci_failures_full.log` was a fetch-failed stub):

   ```
   NEW > 8  js/unit-tests/test_postPRReviewComments.js::file_read#10: 8.7
   ```
   `sanitizeReviewData` at CC 23 exceeds `CRAP_THRESHOLD=8` on complexity alone — no coverage percentage can bring CRAP below CC. I reproduced the ratchet pipeline locally (nyc instrument + pinned crap4js + released baseline).

2. ⚠️ **IMPORTANT — incidental spec mentions demote genuine blockers** (verified live with the shipped regexes): a body containing a real "🚨 BLOCKING: SQL injection…" plus an uncited "(the spec says…)" parenthetical is demoted and the verdict collapses to APPROVE — the inverse failure direction of the hostage problem, and worse.

3. ⚠️ **IMPORTANT — citation detection gaps** (both directions verified): `Policy.java#L61`-style GitHub anchors are not recognized (a *cited* claim loses BLOCKING force — violates AC4), while any `https://` URL counts as a citation (unverified claim keeps BLOCKING force).

4. 💡 Suggestions: duplicate `comment` file references double-count downgrades and drift the census; the downgrade note says "confirm against the cited source" when no citation exists; added require-mapping lines are misaligned (and their 8× duplication is what blew the test-helper CRAP).

The overall design (sanitize before verdict derivation, fail-open guard, cited claims keep force, prompt-side + machine-side halves) is sound and matches the ticket ACs — the issues are in the predicate edges and the complexity budget.
